summary: Mostly not. Buying around the lower band, at the default width or at 2.5 SD, did no better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily. The result that holds up is on 4h in uptrends: price moved more after crossing up through the upper band than after random candles, which comes from volatile timing in a rising window rather than picking direction, and the mirror short did worse than random.

verdicts.use: Buying the bounce off the lower band
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily, as a cross back up through the band, while price sat below it, or with a 2.5 SD band.

verdicts.use: Buying the breakout above the upper band
verdicts.text: Beat random on 4h, but the gap rests on signals on Aug 10–17, 2021, and these crossings fire in volatile candles in a window that rose. Same as random on 1h and daily.

verdicts.use: Shorting the drop back under the upper band
verdicts.text: Worse than random by 0.49% on 4h, and it holds without its strongest stretch, though only at 20 and 100 candles. Same as random on 1h and daily.

verdicts.use: Riding a cross up through the middle band
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. The 4h beat in downtrends rests on two signals on Jan 11–12, 2023.

notes: Going long as price crossed back up through the lower band on 1h gave 5,034 entries in 2,659 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.03% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band. Staying in while price sat below the band enters about twice as often and lands in the same place. A 2.5 SD band fires about half as often and also matched random, as every lower-band setting did on 4h and daily.

Going long as price crossed up through the upper band on 4h beat random entries by 0.51% after 20 candles, and at 10, 50 and 100 candles too. Without the signals on Aug 10–17, 2021 it falls back into the luck band. These crossings fire in volatile candles, in a window where price rose overall, so price moved more after them because of when they fire. On daily the pooled result sat inside the band, and SOL's 11% beat rests on signals between Jan 30, 2021 and Feb 22, 2021, with the same timing caveat.

Split by trend, the 4h upper-band long carries in uptrends: 0.7% ahead of random, and it holds without its strongest stretch. In downtrends it was same as random. The mirror short did 0.49% worse than random pooled and holds without the signals between Dec 29, 2020 and Jan 5, 2021. In uptrends that short was fragile-worse, resting on Aug 10–17, 2021, and in downtrends it showed nothing.

On daily, the short as price crossed back down through the upper band was same as random pooled, but the regimes split. In downtrends it beat random by 5% after 20 days across 45 separate moves, and at 50 and 100 days. It held without its strongest signal on Nov 6, 2022, at the start of the FTX collapse. In uptrends it was same as random, and on SOL it was fragile-worse, resting on signals between Jan 5, 2021 and Feb 25, 2021.

Single stretches can fake a result. On 4h, the middle-band cross beat random by 0.39% in downtrends, but only because of two signals on Jan 11–12, 2023. On daily, the 2.5 SD lower-band bounce looked worse than random in downtrends only because of signals on May 1–12, 2022, during the Terra collapse, and in uptrends it had too few moves to judge. ETH's daily lower-band bounce looked bad only because of signals between Jan 21, 2026 and Feb 6, 2026.

For a long DCA bot, a lower-band start condition times nothing on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work, and you can leave the condition out. The 4h upper-band crossing marks candles after which price moved more, which reads best as a filter beside an uptrend condition, not as a reason to open a long alone. A short bot that opens as price drops back under the 4h upper band traded against price. In downtrends the 4h upper-band long was same as random, so the filter does nothing there.
